cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul presses on to take hold of it. He says he presses on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of him. He's not claiming to be finished, and he's not sitting still either. Friends, that's a man in motion. I'll take a teacher who admits he's still on the road over one who pretends he's already home.

The answer is what is behind. Paul says, "Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead…" (Philippians 3:13). Notice he doesn't list what's behind, so I won't either. His eyes are pointed forward, and he's straining toward it. That's a man who is going somewhere.

The answer is prize. Paul presses on toward the goal to win the prize of God's heavenly calling in Christ Jesus. A goal and a prize go together, and he has both in view. He's not wandering, friends. He knows exactly where he's headed.

The answer is True. Paul says, "And if you think differently about some issue, God will reveal this to you as well." Look who does the revealing: God. Paul isn't promising to win every debate himself. I find that a relief, friends.

The answer is to live up to what we have already attained. Paul says, "Nevertheless, we must live up to what we have already attained." Even where people think differently, there's something already in hand to live by. So you don't have to wait for every question to be settled. You can walk in what you've already got.

The answer is Paul's own. Paul says, "Join one another in following my example, brothers…" (Philippians 3:17). Notice the words "Join one another…" They're meant to follow it together, not each on their own.

The answer is those who walk by the pattern he set. Paul says to carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern "…we set for you." So the examples aren't just Paul. He points past himself to anyone whose walk matches that pattern. Friends, the lesson is to watch how people walk.

The answer is enemies. Paul says, "Many live as enemies of the cross of Christ." That's a heavy word, and he's said it with tears. I think this one is meant to be taken seriously. Let's not rush past it.
The answer is False. Paul says the enemies of the cross have minds "…set on earthly things." He doesn't say heavenly things. Then he turns to what's different about us, and that's the next verse.

The answer is in heaven. Paul says, "But our citizenship is in heaven…" The word "But" matters here. Those other folks have their minds set on earthly things, and Paul points somewhere else. Friends, heaven is the citizenship he names for us.
The answer is the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul says we eagerly await a Savior from there, "…the Lord Jesus Christ…" He names Him plainly. No guessing needed, friends. The One we're waiting on is Jesus.

The answer is glorious. Paul says Jesus will transform our lowly bodies "…to be like His glorious body." Our bodies are called lowly, and His is called glorious. And the change happens by the power that enables Him to subject all things to Himself. I'd say that's quite the upgrade.
The answer is True. Paul says, "…my brothers, whom I love and long for, my joy and crown…" That's a man telling them he loves them and longs for them. I'd love to be called that by somebody, friends.

The answer is to stand firm in the Lord. Paul says, "…that is how you must stand firm in the Lord, my beloved." He ends by calling them beloved, which fits everything he said before it. Standing firm is the last thing he asks of them here.
